entries.title: A destructor loses its whole fs:[0] frame when the body only calls extern "C" functions
entries.symptom: Candidate starts with 'push esi' instead of 'push -1'; no .text$x/.xdata$x; function is ~40 bytes short. Example: 0x53fcc0 was 160 bytes vs 207.
entries.cause: VC6 /GX does not create a try region for calls declared extern "C". If the destructor has no virtual call, no member destructor, and no C++-linkage call, it emits no EH frame at all.
entries.source_pattern: Declare the CRT-like callees with C++ linkage in the TU: 'void Mem_Free(void *);' and 'int CRT_Fclose(void *);'. A throwing call in the body restores the two-state unwind frame.
entries.counter_pattern: 'extern "C" void __cdecl Mem_Free(void *);' plus plain extern "C" calls in the body.

entries.title: Missing 'mov [esp+state],0' before an inlined member destructor
entries.symptom: Two unwind states and correct funclets exist, but the candidate never writes state 0 before the inlined member destruction; first difference is that store. Examples: 0x5408b0 and 0x541f30 (parked as 29-byte near misses).
entries.cause: The member destructor's call was declared extern "C" and is treated as nothrow, so VC6 keeps state 1 active through the inline. A potentially throwing member destructor makes the compiler deactivate the outer state first.
entries.source_pattern: Give the member destructor's callee C++ linkage: 'void Mem_Free(void *);' rather than 'extern "C" void __cdecl Mem_Free(void *);'.
entries.counter_pattern: extern "C" declaration for the member destructor's free/close call.

entries.title: COM-style virtual calls push 'this'; declare the interface methods __stdcall
entries.symptom: Candidate emits 'mov ecx,[obj]; call *off(ecx)' but the original emits 'push obj; mov ecx,[obj]; call *off(ecx)' (and pushes stack arguments first).
entries.cause: A thiscall virtual method receives 'this' in ECX and needs no push. A __stdcall COM method receives 'this' as the first stack argument, so VC6 pushes it.
entries.source_pattern: virtual void __stdcall Release(); virtual int __stdcall Query();
entries.counter_pattern: virtual void Release(); (thiscall) for a COM-style interface slot.

entries.title: Multi-level destructor chains need inline ancestor destructors and an out-of-line target
entries.symptom: Derived destructor candidate is much shorter and contains a call to the base destructor; the original inlines the whole chain and has one EH frame with several states. Example: 0x541790 was 96 bytes vs 225.
entries.cause: VC6 does not inline an ancestor destructor that is defined out-of-line in the same TU (the 169-byte List body is not inlined). Defining ancestors inside their class bodies makes them inline into the derived destructor.
entries.source_pattern: Define each ancestor destructor inside its class ('virtual ~Base() { body }'). Declare the target destructor in the class and define it out-of-line after the class definitions; that forces emission of the entry COMDAT plus ancestor vtables and deleting destructors.
entries.counter_pattern: All destructors defined out-of-line, or all inline (the target COMDAT then may not be emitted at all).

entries.title: List teardown order: free the node before storing the next head
entries.symptom: Four-byte shift and an extra head reload; original keeps next in a register across the call: 'mov edi,[eax+4]; push eax; call; mov [head],edi; test edi,edi; jne'. Candidate stores head before the call and reloads it after.
entries.cause: Source order changes the scheduler's store placement. 'head = next; free(node);' stores first; 'next = head->next; free(head); head = next;' frees first and matches.
entries.source_pattern: while (head != 0) { Node *next = head->next; Mem_Free(head); head = next; }
entries.counter_pattern: while (head != 0) { Node *node = head; head = node->next; Mem_Free(node); }

entries.title: VC6 materializes a shared zero in EBX ('xor ebx,ebx; cmp bl,al')
entries.symptom: Original uses 'xor ebx,ebx' and then 'cmp bl,al', 'cmp ebx,eax', 'push ebx', 'mov [member],ebx'. Candidate uses 'test al,al', 'test eax,eax', 'push 0' and immediate stores.
entries.cause: The zero is reused across byte/pointer compares, an integer argument, and member stores. VC6 hoists it into EBX when the surrounding code makes those uses one common value; it is usually a consequence of correct EH/linkage shape rather than a separate source variable.
entries.source_pattern: Recover the natural multi-use zero first (throwable calls, member destructor, several zero stores). Do not add a fake 'int zero = 0;' to steer allocation.
entries.counter_pattern: Literal-only uses that the instruction selector folds to immediate/test forms.

entries.title: Do not hand-bind $L/$T anchors; the matcher derives them from the PE
entries.symptom: EH funclet or .xdata$x relocations remain unresolved when a recipe binds section-local $L/$T labels by hand.
entries.cause: tools/match_decomp.py derives the original EH section anchors from the target PE's unwind tables and text spans. Hand bindings fight that derivation and are not independent evidence.
entries.source_pattern: Compile with /GX, pass '--strict --auto-symbols', and bind only real functions, vtables, and data symbols. Let the matcher place $L/$T anchors.

entries.title: Generator field arrays need an explicit size or the next field shifts by four
entries.symptom: A member field lands 4 bytes too far (e.g. TrackBuffer field8 at +0xc instead of +0x8); one-byte diff at the first member access.
entries.cause: generate_destructor_family.field_block advances the cursor by the field's 'size' (default 4). A declaration like 'char pad0[8];' without "size": 8 advances by 4 and inserts an unintended 4-byte pad before the next field.
entries.counter_pattern: {"decl": "char pad0[8];", "offset": 0} followed by a field at offset 8.

entries.title: Two filter fields in one condition must be materialized as locals
entries.symptom: Original loads both record fields before the first branch ('mov edx,[eax+8]; mov ecx,[eax+4]; cmp edx,edi'). Candidate folds them into memory operands ('cmp edi,[eax+8]'; 'cmp ebp,[eax+4]') and is four bytes short; the first visible difference is the short jump displacement.
entries.cause: VC6 treats each single-use field comparison as a memory operand. Naming both fields as locals forces the loads into registers and keeps the second value live across the first branch, which is the shipped schedule.
entries.source_pattern: int rf = record->field; int ri = record->index; if ((rf == field || field == -1) && (index == -1 || index == ri)) { ... }

entries.title: FP accumulation with a memory array element needs a value local to fix operand order
entries.symptom: Candidate emits 'flds [total]; fadds [record+col*4]' while the original emits 'flds [record+col*4]; fadds [total]'; first difference is in the single-column path.
entries.cause: Both operands are memory. VC6 chooses the accumulator as the first load unless the array element is first made a value; the value local forces the record load before the accumulator load.
